---
title: "Underwater glider"
description: "Buoyancy-driven vehicle for energy-efficient, long-duration observation."
---

<span class="status">Modeled and simulated. Hardware in development.</span>

Underwater gliders change their buoyancy to dive and climb, and shift an internal mass to control pitch, so they use little energy. We study how to make them last longer on a battery.

## What we have shown, in simulation

An energy-aware, event-triggered geometric controller formulated on the special Euclidean group SE(3). In simulation on a Seawing-class glider model, it used more than 45% less energy and 31% fewer control updates than a conventional time-triggered controller over the same mission, with a modest increase in tracking error.

## In development

A compact prototype with a buoyancy engine and a moving-mass mechanism. It has not been wet tested.
